deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a page of German lecture or study notes on ancient Israelite history. It continues the previous page (Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, the sojourn in Egypt) and leads into the next (conquest of Canaan under Joshua).

Content, in paraphrase:
(a) The tribe divided into 12 branches named after Jacob's sons. They lived quietly in Egypt for a long time. When they became formidable to Egypt, they were forced (or the Egyptians tried to force them) to adopt another way of life.
(b) The reasons for Moses' legislation:
  1. By observing these laws the Israelites should remain permanently a distinct people, separate from other nations.
  2. They should form a state and so pass over to agriculture and fixed settlements.
(c) To reach these goals Moses made faith in the national God Jehovah the centre of his legislation. Everyone in the nation shared in this cult. As long as the worship of the God lasted, the nation could not fall apart. The worship was precisely prescribed, and the sanctuary was the centre of the whole nation.
(d) A new heading, 'Zweite Periode' (Second Period), underlined: from the founding of their state to the beginning of the monarchical constitution.

The periodisation (republic after Joshua, c. 1500–1000 BC, on the next page) and the stress on Moses' law as a political-religious device for national cohesion are typical of late-18th and early-19th-century Göttingen universal-history lectures, e.g. the Heeren or Eichhorn school. There is no derivation, formula, number theory, astronomy or geodesy to reconstruct. The handwriting and genre suggest these are notes in the Gauss family or Nachlass papers (possibly by a child or student) rather than Gauss's own scientific work. That attribution is uncertain.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors to report. Historically, the statements simply reflect the biblical narrative as received in contemporary lectures.
Grammatical slip in the machine transcription: 'war sie gezwungen' does not agree with its subject. The image more plausibly reads 'wollte man sie zwingen' (see transcription corrections).

Line 'Alle die zu der Nation gehörten, hatten Theil an diesem Cultus': 'Cultus' is written at the right margin, squeezed in above the following line, not on its own line.

'so lange der Dienst des Gottes bestand blieb': the image has 'Solange der Dienst des Gottes bestand blieb' (possibly 'fortbestand' or 'bestehen blieb'). 'so' is written at the end of the line before 'lange konnte die Nation nicht zerfallen'.
'ging er davon aus' has an interlinear correction near 'aus' at the right margin; the reading is otherwise plausible.
Folio number '17' in the upper right corner is confirmed.
